rationale:
Evidence: iteration 0 scored 89 and iteration 1 scored 124.4 (best so far), but all runs leave the track. Iteration 1 (kp 3.0, kd 0.5, track 0.10 m, 7 sensors at 10 mm spacing) reached progress 0.50 on the oval, with steering_oscillation of 0.28 and max_error at the 0.06 m limit. Iteration 2 (kp 2.0, kd 0.2, track 0.14 m, 16 mm sensors at 15 mm spacing) fell to 48.9, with progress about 0.12 on every track. So iteration 2 was too sluggish, not too oscillatory, and iteration 1 was too aggressive. My estimate of effective steering authority per metre of line offset is kp x (outer weight / outer x) / (wheel_track / 350), which gives about 150/m for iteration 0 (turn rate about 1250), 200/m for iteration 1 (about 2000) and 89/m for iteration 2 (about 640). The good operating point lies between iterations 1 and 2, and iteration 0 was closest to it on turn authority but had too few sensors.

Changes: (1) Keep the 7-sensor, 12 mm footprint array, which gives smoother readings than 10 mm, but tighten spacing to 12 mm (x = -0.036 to +0.036) so the array still covers offsets of about 4 cm. Weights stay linear, -2 to +2, so the signal is about 56 per metre of offset. (2) kp raised from 2.0 to 3.5, giving about 195 per metre of offset and turn authority of about 1600 per metre on a 0.12 m track. This sits between iterations 1 and 2 on the authority scale. (3) kd set to 0.4, between the 0.2 and 0.5 values that were tried, to damp the oscillation seen at kd 0.5 without leaving the signal undamped. (4) wheel_track set to 0.12 m, between 0.10 and 0.14. (5) base_speed set to 1.3, between 1.2 and 1.4, which gives progress without much line-loss risk on the bends. (6) ki stays at 0 to avoid windup on the curves. Mass 0.6 kg, body 0.15 x 0.12 m and wheel radius 0.03 m are unchanged. Sensor y stays at 0.03 m.

Expected result: progress above 0.5 on the s-bend and slalom, line_loss_events at 1 or fewer, steering_oscillation near 0.2, and at least some oval completions. Hypotheses: (a) the 12 mm footprint array keeps the line in view through bends; (b) the turn authority in the middle of the range avoids both the oscillation of iteration 1 and the sluggishness of iteration 2. Failure signs: oscillation above 0.25 means kp or kd is still too high; progress stuck near 0.3 with few line losses means kp is too low or speed too high. Next measurements: progress and line_loss_events show whether the array holds the line; max_error and steering_oscillation show whether the gains are balanced; completion_time shows the speed margin.
